subject: Warning and fatal error in stratified analysis

messages.author: 4274ca4414fad7f1
messages.subject: Warning and fatal error in stratified analysis
parts:
​Hi everyone!

I am a beginner user on the Biogeobers package. For days, I have been trying to run a stratified analysis using my own data set on BiogeoBears and I have got stuck since while on this warning and Fatal error (below).

WARNING in chainsaw2: input tree had a 'root.edge', which crashes chainsaw2. Setting original_tree$root.edge=NULL.
FATAL ERROR in section_the_tree(): Your tree has 4 fossil tips older than 0.1 my!
But you have not turned on fossils by setting 'cut_fossils=FALSE' in section_the_tree().
Fossil tip names listed below:
[1] "Fossil_one"  "Fossil_two"     
[3] "Fossil_three" "Fossil_four".
Error in section_the_tree(input = BioGeoBEARS_run_object, make_master_table = TRUE,  : 
Further: Warning message: In section_the_tree(input = BioGeoBEARS_run_object, make_master_table = TRUE,  : WARNING in chainsaw2: input tree had a 'root.edge', which crashes chainsaw2. Setting original_tree$root.edge=NULL.

Please, could someone give me some advice on how to solve these problems? 

Thanks in advance.​

--

messages.author: 115d05260b0c341a
messages.subject: Re: [BioGeoBEARS] Warning and fatal error in stratified analysis
parts:
Hi -- the root thing is just a warning, you can ignore.

For the fatal error, like the error message message says:

Go to the line of the script with section_the_tree()

Add the option cut_fossils=FALSE to that command.  cut_fossils=FALSE means you won't cut out the fossils. 

Re-run it.

Cheers!
Nick

PS (This option exists  because for various reasons, including minor computer number rounding issues, people can have tree tips that don't quite come up to 0.000 million years before present, but they don't intend these to be fossils.)
